第 16 章 Developing Communication Patterns发展沟通模式

Travis Donia / 特拉维斯·多尼亚

— 第 55 页 —

Organizations which design systems are constrained to produce designs which are copies of the communication structures of these organizations. —Conway's Law, Melvin Conway

设计系统的组织，其产生的设计等同于组织内的沟通结构。——康威定律，梅尔文·康威

Your job as a manager is to help your team work together effectively. Because the challenge is bigger than any one person, what your team ships will reflect the communication that happens. By developing communication patterns within and around your team, you'll improve what you ship. Here are some ideas on how to begin:

作为经理，你的工作是帮助团队高效协作。因为挑战大过任何个人，团队交付的东西会反映团队内部的沟通方式。通过在团队内部和周围发展沟通模式，你会改善交付质量。以下是一些入门建议：

Be a good listener做一个好的倾听者

First, you need to understand what communication patterns are established, so look for the conversations that are already happening. Who is talking to whom, and what about? This will take time. At the beginning, the team won't automatically trust you and might be guarded. Respect that. To build trust, you'll need to be present whenever you're asked for and prove yourself as an active, empathetic, and useful listener. As you build trust, you'll be let in to more conversations. The same is true for communication outside your team. As you work with other parts of your company, you'll identify the conversations you have a stake in, and you can earn the trust to be invited in the future.

首先，你需要了解已经建立了什么沟通模式，所以去观察已经在发生的对话。谁在和谁说话？在说什么？这需要时间。一开始，团队不会自动信任你，可能会有戒心。尊重这一点。要建立信任，你需要随叫随到，证明自己是一个积极、有同理心、有用的倾听者。随着信任的建立，你会被邀请参与更多对话。团队外部的沟通也是如此。当你和公司其他部门合作时，你会识别出你有利益相关的对话，你可以赢得信任、未来被邀请参与。

Look ahead向前看

You can further earn the team's trust and make it more efficient by anticipating the questions it will have. For instance, wherever your team members' work overlaps, they will need to be aligned on how their work will interface. Junior team members are not always going to plan for that, and there's a risk of wasted effort if an agreed-upon interface isn't defined early enough. By anticipating that, you can ensure that they're communicating with one another early enough in the process to build toward the same goal.

你可以通过预判团队会有的问题来进一步赢得信任并提高效率。例如，只要团队成员的工作有重叠，他们就需要在工作接口上对齐。初级成员不会总是主动计划这个，如果不够早地定义好接口，就有浪费精力的风险。通过预判，你可以确保他们在过程中足够早地互相沟通，朝着同一个目标努力。

— 第 56 页 —

Be a hub做一个枢纽

There are only so many questions you can answer, so it's important to learn to route questions to others. For instance, maybe it's better for a member of your team to chat with a PM directly: the PM might be more familiar with the implementation and could answer more of the team's questions. This is a powerful tool, but use it with care. Not everyone will love answering questions, and even for those who do, there's still a limit to the number of questions one person can answer.

你能回答的问题有限，所以学会把问题路由给别人很重要。比如，也许让团队成员直接和 PM 聊更好：PM 可能更熟悉实现细节，能回答更多团队的问题。这是一个强大的工具，但要小心使用。不是每个人都喜欢回答问题，即使是喜欢的人，一个人能回答的问题数量也有限。

Provide visibility提供可见性

Your job is more than just handling questions; you've have a mandate from the wider organization and direction that you need to give the team. You're responsible for providing visibility to that mandate and its related workstreams. Smart people often work better when they know why something is important, so connect the dots between day-to-day work and the big picture when new requests are made. How does fixing a bug improve someone's life or grow the business? Help the team understand where it fits in within the company and where the company fits in within the world. Equally important is helping the company understand the strengths and value of your team. Visibility runs both ways.

你的工作不只是处理问题；你从更广泛的组织那里得到了授权和方向，需要传达给团队。你有责任让这个授权和相关工作流变得可见。聪明的人知道某件事为什么重要时往往工作得更好，所以在新需求来的时候，把日常工作和大局连起来。修一个 bug 怎么改善了某人的生活或发展了业务？帮团队理解它在公司里的位置，以及公司在世界上的位置。同样重要的是帮公司理解你团队的优势和价值。可见性是双向的。

Protect your team's time保护团队的时间

An endless stream of meetings, chats, and emails consumes valuable time; the code will not write itself. It's just as important to help your team focus so that it has time to do work. It's usually worth asking yourself—and others—is this a good use of time? One of the easiest ways you can make the team more productive is by finding ways to ensure that communication happens without requiring team members to break their flow. This often is why standups happen at the beginning of the day—it means less time lost context switching. "No meeting Tuesdays" is the same idea.

没完没了的会议、聊天和邮件消耗宝贵时间；代码不会自己写出来。帮团队保持专注、有时间干活同样重要。通常值得问你自己——以及别人——这是对时间的好的利用吗？让团队更高效的最简单方法之一是找到方式确保沟通发生而不需要团队成员打断心流。这就是为什么站会通常在一天开始时开——意味着更少的上下文切换时间损失。「无会议周二」是同样的思路。

Find the question behind the question找到问题背后的问题

As you grow as a leader, you will be brought into ambiguous situations, and it will become more difficult to know what you can share. The correct answer might not be obvious, and there will be reasons why you cannot share everything. Resist the urge to let this be a reason to depersonalize your relationships or to ask the team to "just trust me." Instead, use those moments to empathize. Listen hard and understand the question behind the question. You might not be able to give the team the sensitive information it's asking for, but you can earn trust by demonstrating that you understand team members' concerns.

随着你作为领导者成长，你会被带入模糊的情境，会越来越难知道你能分享什么。正确答案可能不明显，也有你不能分享一切的理由。不要让这个成为把关系去个人化、或者让团队「相信我就好」的理由。相反，用这些时刻来共情。认真倾听，理解问题背后的问题。你可能无法给团队他们要的敏感信息，但你可以通过展示你理解团队成员的关切来赢得信任。

— 第 57 页 —

As your team places more trust in you, you'll find yourself cc'd on more emails and drawn into more conversations. You'll be asked to provide context more often. You'll be brought problems and given the opportunity to help edit and focus the communication that's happening. Notice the outcomes of the conversations that happen when you're not in the room. These are all signs that you're establishing communication patterns, and that's one of the most important things we can do as managers.

随着团队越来越信任你，你会发现自己被抄送到更多邮件、被拉入更多对话。你会更经常被要求提供上下文。问题会被带到你面前，你有机会帮助编辑和聚焦正在进行的沟通。注意那些你不在场时发生的对话的结果。这些都是你在建立沟通模式的信号，而这是作为经理我们能做的最重要的事情之一。
